# Dad's Telescope

> An observing assistant for one specific telescope: a Celestron StarSense
> Explorer 8" Dobsonian (203 mm, 1200 mm, f/6). It reports what is worth
> observing tonight from a given location, and exactly which eyepiece,
> magnification and filter to use.

The number shown is an Observability Score (0-100), not a probability of seeing
an object. Seeing and transparency are never reported, because no free data
source supplies them; missing weather lowers confidence rather than being
replaced by an estimate.

## Data sources

- [Astronomy Engine](https://github.com/cosinekitty/astronomy): MIT-licensed ephemeris used for all positions, rise/set times, twilight and Moon calculations.
- [JPL Horizons](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/): independent reference; positions are validated against it to within one arcminute.
- [OpenNGC](https://github.com/mattiaverga/OpenNGC): CC-BY-SA-4.0 deep-sky catalogue supplying coordinates, magnitudes, angular sizes and surface brightness.
- [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/): CC-BY-4.0 hourly forecast, the primary weather source.
- [US National Weather Service API](https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api): public-domain fallback weather source.

## Optional

- [Kasten & Young airmass](https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.28.004735): the 1989 formula used for atmospheric extinction.
